rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to capture all 10 compounds and identify the elution window and limiting pairs. A moderate gradient duration and temperature provide a useful baseline for improving resolution while targeting a last peak within 10 minutes.

Make the gradient slightly shallower to test whether the limiting pair responds to slope, while keeping the last peak near the 10-minute target. Holding the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed isolates this effect.

Raise temperature by 5 C to test selectivity for the remaining unresolved pair while shortening retention. Keeping the gradient unchanged isolates the temperature effect; only a modest resolution gain is needed to reach CRF 1.0.

The limiting pair converged strongly from 40 to 45 C; testing 55 C may separate it again after an elution-order reversal. Other neighboring pairs appear to have enough resolution margin, and higher temperature should keep the last peak below 10 minutes.

Use a modestly steeper gradient to improve the limiting pair after its apparent elution-order reversal, while shortening the run. This smaller slope change should preserve the neighboring pair’s resolution margin better than shortening to 12 minutes with phi1 unchanged.

Injection 5 reached the maximum CRF; now test a slightly steeper gradient for a shorter fully resolved run. The observed slope response suggests the limiting pair may improve slightly, while the neighboring pair should remain near or above R = 1.5.

The maximum CRF is already secured, so test a substantially faster method. Higher temperature and a steeper gradient may move the close middle peaks through an elution-order reversal and restore separation on the other side; this run will test whether full resolution survives.

Shorten the gradient at fixed temperature to test whether the newly limiting pair separates further after its apparent order reversal. Injection 6 remains the fully resolved fallback while this run explores a faster method.

Return near the fully resolved injection 6 and raise the starting organic fraction to test a shorter elution window without aggressive gradient compression. This probes whether changing the solvent window improves the two marginal middle pairs while retaining CRF 1.0.

Test a narrower solvent window to recover the resolution lost when raising the starting organic fraction. The shallower slope should help the limiting middle pair, while the higher starting fraction may keep the last peak earlier than in injection 6.

Keep the starting fraction below the level that further compressed the limiting pair, and flatten the gradient relative to injection 9. This should improve that pair while retaining the other pair’s resolution, targeting CRF 1.0 with more margin than injection 6.

With CRF 1.0 already achieved, test a distinctly cooler selectivity regime combined with a shorter gradient. Cooling may separate the middle cluster through different elution-order changes, offering another route to a faster fully resolved method.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction at 60 C moves the limiting middle pair far enough beyond its order reversal to regain baseline resolution. A 10-minute gradient provides more separation space than the previous fast 60 C runs while targeting earlier final elution than injection 6.

Increase only the starting organic fraction to test whether the limiting middle pair separates further beyond its order reversal. Watch the first two peaks closely, since their resolution may become limiting as initial retention decreases.

Return to the successful 55 C selectivity and use a slope between injections 9 and 11, closer to the fully resolved injection 11. This targets baseline resolution of both limiting pairs with a shorter last-peak time than injection 11.

Trim injection 6’s unused high-organic segment while preserving its starting composition, gradient slope, and temperature. Its last peak exited near 0.57 organic, so ending at 0.65 should retain the maximum CRF and approximately 7.60-minute last-peak time with a shorter programmed gradient.

Test an intermediate cooler selectivity regime using the fully resolved solvent program from injection 11. This isolates temperature and checks whether 35 C offers a useful alternative separation pattern; the maximum-score 55 C method remains secured.

Raise temperature from injection 17 by 5 C to separate its limiting pair while checking that the neighboring pair remains resolved. This isolates temperature and tests an alternative route to maximum CRF with potentially better resolution margin.

Reduce the gradient slope from 0.0625 to 0.055 organic fraction per minute to improve the slope-sensitive limiting pair. This targets full resolution with the last peak just below 10 minutes, potentially providing a maximum-score alternative at 40 C.

Shift injection 19’s solvent window upward while preserving its gradient slope to shorten retention. This tests whether the fully resolved 40 C method can be accelerated without losing the limiting pair’s resolution.

Test a small increase in slope from the fastest fully resolved method, injection 6, to locate the speed–resolution boundary. The last peak should elute earlier, but the pair previously at R = 1.59 is at risk; the maximum-CRF method remains available.

With maximum CRF already achieved, test a shallower gradient for greater resolution margin at 55 C. Relative to injection 10, this should improve the limiting middle pair while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Slightly reduce the slope from injection 22 to improve its limiting pair while targeting final elution below 10 minutes. The maximum CRF is already secured; this tests a method with greater resolution margin.

Use a different gradient endpoint and duration while preserving the successful slope of 0.075 organic fraction per minute. All peaks should elute before the gradient ends, reproducing the maximum CRF and approximately 7.60-minute last-peak time of injections 6 and 16.

Use a slope between injections 22 and 23 and trim the unused high-organic portion. This targets CRF 1.000 with a minimum resolution near 1.67 and final elution around 9.3 minutes, providing more resolution margin than the fastest successful method.
